title: Hazard trail
subtitle: Build a readable hazard trail with a reachable response and a useful recovery.
summary: Movement leaves a temporary dangerous path behind the boss or player.
overview: Movement leaves a temporary dangerous path behind the boss or player, making recent trajectories constrain the next route through the arena.
learning: Tune the signal, commitment, geometry, response, and recovery of a hazard trail as one rule.

steps.title: Can the player read the complete rule?
steps.body: Show where the trail begins, its exact width, and how it expires; the moving source and persistent residue need distinct visual states.

steps.title: Is the intended response reachable?
steps.body: The player curves movement to place the trail safely, crosses behind its expiration edge, or uses open space before routes close.

steps.title: Does recovery create a useful outcome?
steps.body: Trail segments expire in placement order and reopen the route from oldest to newest, making recovery of arena space predictable.

mistakes.title: A trail that appears behind the visual source with no placement preview punishes movement the player has already committed to
mistakes.body: A trail that appears behind the visual source with no placement preview punishes movement the player has already committed to.

mistakes.title: The cue and active geometry disagree
mistakes.body: If the visible hazard trail cue promises a different area or timing, the player cannot carry the learned rule into the next cycle.

designNotes.title: Tune the complete rule
designNotes.body: Balance trail lifetime, width, source speed, turn radius, and arena area so route choices matter without sealing every exit.

designNotes.title: Escalate one variable at a time
designNotes.body: Increase persistence or add a second trail source, then cap overlap and preserve a readable expiration order.

designNotes.title: Prove the recovery
designNotes.body: Trail segments expire in placement order and reopen the route from oldest to newest, making recovery of arena space predictable.

story.title: What the mechanic communicates
story.body: Movement leaves a temporary dangerous path behind the boss or player, making recent trajectories constrain the next route through the arena. The encounter uses that rule as a short promise: a visible signal, a committed action, and a result the player can verify.

adaptation.title: Adapt it to the player verbs
adaptation.body: The player curves movement to place the trail safely, crosses behind its expiration edge, or uses open space before routes close. Balance trail lifetime, width, source speed, turn radius, and arena area so route choices matter without sealing every exit.

distinction.title: Keep the mechanic distinct
distinction.body: A trail that appears behind the visual source with no placement preview punishes movement the player has already committed to. Do not hide that distinction behind extra effects or tracking that the announced rule does not contain.

lensNotes.body: The signal must reveal the relevant timing and geometry before commitment.
The complete player extent and the active region determine whether the route is real.
The response uses an ordinary supported verb and produces an observable result.
At least one route remains reachable with the movement options available at this point.
